concept: MongoDB driver topology discovery and server selection
summary: Source-anchored research for MongoDB driver topology discovery and server selection. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The load-balancer specification defines an explicit exception: with loadBalanced=true, the topology remains LoadBalanced, contains a single LoadBalancer server description, and starts no monitoring connection. An SRV URI in this mode must not be polled for SRV changes. (low confidence)

For a primary description whose address is already in the topology, whose replica-set name matches the accepted name or establishes it when unset, and which passes the electionId and setVersion stale-primary checks, SDAM adds previously unknown addresses from its hosts, passives, and arbiters lists and removes servers absent from those lists. An existing-address non-primary description with a matching or newly established replica-set name and no known primary can add members, but does not prune the other members using its host list. (low confidence)

For a primary description whose address is already in the topology, whose replica-set name matches the accepted name or establishes it when unset, and which passes the electionId and setVersion stale-primary checks, the SDAM algorithm adds previously unknown addresses from its hosts, passives, and arbiters lists and begins monitoring them; it removes servers absent from those lists and stops monitoring them. (low confidence)

When a new primary is discovered, SDAM marks the previous primary Unknown and requires a multi-threaded client to request an immediate check of that server; it explicitly forbids clearing that old primary's connection pool for this transition. (low confidence)

Grafana's MongoDB troubleshooting guidance lists unreachable replica-set members as a possible cause of selection failures and recommends making all members reachable, because drivers contact secondaries for discovery. This is troubleshooting guidance, not a rule that any unavailable secondary prevents every operation. (high confidence)

If a write to the known primary fails with a network error other than a timeout, the specification describes marking that server Unknown and changing ReplicaSetWithPrimary to ReplicaSetNoPrimary. An established-connection network timeout alone must not mark the server Unknown. (low confidence)

Grafana advises checking DNS resolution and reachability of replica-set members when its MongoDB data source reports selection errors; the Databasus issue reporter separately documents discovery of an internal Kubernetes hostname followed by DNS failure and ReplicaSetNoPrimary. (medium confidence)

The TypeORM issue reporter traced a historical connection failure to omission of directConnection from validOptionNames, and later stated that newer TypeORM versions fixed that omission. This report does not establish a current TypeORM defect. (low confidence)

If multi-threaded server selection finds no suitable server, it requests an immediate topology check and waits for a topology change or the selection timeout; timing out raises a server selection error. (low confidence)

Monitoring behavior is driver-specific: PHP performs monitoring between application operations; the selection specification requires single-threaded drivers to refresh topology during selection rather than through background monitoring. (medium confidence)

Single-threaded drivers update topology during server selection rather than monitoring it in the background. With serverSelectionTryOnce true, selection timeouts have no effect and a stale topology or failed first selection triggers a single immediate check; with false, selection loops until success or timeout. (low confidence)

The discovery model differs by deployment: one replica-set seed can reveal the other members; a sharded client starts from mongos seeds and may discover additional mongos hosts through SRV polling. (low confidence)

The topology initialization table maps direct connection to Single; with direct connection disabled, a replica-set name yields ReplicaSetNoPrimary, while no replica-set name yields Unknown. (low confidence)
Receiving a Mongos description changes an Unknown topology to Sharded. A Sharded topology retains Unknown or Mongos descriptions and removes other server types. (low confidence)

Multi-threaded and asynchronous selection must release an operation once a suitable server is available, without waiting for every server to be discovered. If selection finds no suitable server, it requests an immediate topology check and waits for a topology change or selection timeout. (low confidence)

Load-balanced mode requires a loadBalanced field in the connection handshake; if the server hello response lacks serviceId, the driver must raise an exception that the server does not support this mode. (low confidence)
For each server check, SDAM processes the outcome, whether successful or unsuccessful, into a server description and uses it to update the topology description. (low confidence)

In the SDAM example where a primary is reached through an external IP but advertises only internal IPs, the client replaces the external address with the internal address and temporarily enters ReplicaSetNoPrimary until a primary is available through its topology description. (low confidence)
For multi-threaded or asynchronous monitoring, selection must unblock once a suitable server is found; the driver must not wait for discovery of all servers to finish. (low confidence)
